ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a quadrilateral, with vertices labeled in order as Q, T, S, R; inside, two diagonals QS and RT are drawn, and they intersect at point P. Point P is located on diagonal QS, dividing QS into two segments QP and PS, and is also located on diagonal RT, dividing RT into two segments TP and PR. Then reason: If this quadrilateral is a parallelogram, then the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Therefore on diagonal QS there is QP = PS. The problem gives QP = 2y - 6, PS = 5y - 12, so set 2y - 6 = 5y - 12. Solve the equation: 2y - 6 = 5y - 12, transposing terms gives 6 = 3y, therefore y = 2.
